title: Same Drone, No Pilot: Inside the AI Grand Prix
description: In Anduril's AI Grand Prix, teams write software that flies identical Neros drones with no human pilot. Estonian startup Remanguys says it reached the finals using single-camera vision; that is a company claim.

beats.text: Identical drones. Only code can win.
beats.vo: What if every racing drone were identical, and only the software could win?

beats.text: Racing drones with no human pilot
points: One Estonian team uses one camera
beats.vo: In Anduril's A I Grand Prix, teams write software that flies identical drones, with no human pilot. Estonian startup Remanguys says its code flies on a single camera, without G P S or lidar. That is the company's own claim.
Follow for a daily dose of engineering.

caption:
Same drone. No pilot. Only code. 🏁
In Anduril's AI Grand Prix every team flies identical drones, so the software decides. Estonia's Remānguys says it reached the finals using one camera, no GPS or LiDAR (their claim).
Why it matters: fair hardware shows what the software really does.
